newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea crude dips on German sales, low U.S. demand.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea crude dips on German sales, low U.S. demand.

text.p: North Sea cash crude markets slipped lower as Brent faltered after a U.S. Gulf bound ULCC was filled and on news that the German government planned to sell some of its oil reserves, traders said.
Brent CFDs eased a couple of cents for next week's dates while the following three weeks lost between 7 and 10 cents a barrel.
Physical business was thin, with players trying to work out the participants in a number of private deals from Wednesday.

A Brent loading July 23-25 moved from a trader to either a Norwegian or a French buyer at August Brent "plus a lot," on Wednesday dealers said. The previous Brent deal, also on Wednesday, was done at August +10 cents a barrel.

The Norwegian buyer was now believed to have filled the ULCC he fixed for July 21, with purchasers for the contents already lined up. Brent prices may now slip but a tight physical market should provide a floor, dealers added.
One Brent cargo, loading July 25-27, was clocked to Texaco at the five o'clock deadline, traders said.
Late July Oseberg and Gullfaks A cargoes were also believed traded on Wednesday but prices were being kept from the market.

A smattering of July cargoes was all that was left from the month, with three Forties cargoes left, some Statfjord barrels, a Troll and some Draugen thought available and traders beginning to think of next month's loading programmes.
Loading programmes for August are due to be released over the next few days.
Contracts for difference were also confidentially traded on Thursday. Inter-month spreads lost a cent or two, with Aug/Sept trading at -10 cents and Sept/Oct done on legs at -16 cents.

Some strength was thought to have crept into the northern sour crude market, with a trader heard to have bought Baltic sour barrels loading July 23-25 at 20 cents below Dated Brent on Wednesday, basis Rotterdam.
A British major sold some 300,000 barrels of Ventspils sour on Thursday to a Rotterdam refiner, for mid-July delivery, at dated Brent -25 cents.

Turkey's tender for 300,000 tonnes of sour crude was still the only focus in the Mediterranean, with Russian Urals, Syrian Light and Iranian Heavy all believed offered. The tender closes on Friday and results are due on Monday.
Offers were heard around the -55 to -60 cents level, with most traders doubting Turkey's Tupras would take all it requested with numbers so high.
The continued absence of Iraqi barrels has prompted Nigerian National Petroleum Corp to raise its crude contract formula prices for August by between five and 14 cents a barrel, trade sources said.

Two cargoes of Brass River traded at dated Brent +50 cents on Wednesday, loading in first and second decade August respectively, with a Cabinda Zaire, loading August 1-5, traded at a price believed between $1.10 and $1.40.
A second decade Qua Iboe was believed traded into South Africa on Thursday but the price was not known.
